clauses.reason: Terminated by Executive Order 10011, signed October 22, 1948 (published October 26, 1948), paragraph 3(b) of which orders that Executive Order 9870 of July 8, 1947, and Executive Order 9982 of July 29, 1948, are hereby revoked. The order states no delayed effective date, so the effective date is the signing date, 1948-10-22. Executive Order 9982 extended and continued the provisions of Executive Order 9870 (foreign service allowances and allotments) to and including June 30, 1949, effective as of July 1, 1948. That own-terms end date (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end the extension when July 1, 1949 begins) was not reached because the express revocation came first. The proviso in paragraph 3(b) keeps rules and regulations prescribed under the revoked orders in effect until superseded under paragraph 3(a); it does not extend the revoked order itself.

inventory_overrides.reason: The dossier clause begins with the fragment 1949. and the effective-date sentence and omits the operative sentence that extends Executive Order 9870 to and including June 30, 1949; the corrected clause runs from the order heading through the effective-date sentence.

savings.reason: Paragraph 3(b) of Executive Order 10011 keeps existing rules and regulations prescribed under Executive Orders 9870 and 9982 in effect until superseded as provided in paragraph 3(a), and paragraph 1 of that order delegates the underlying statutory powers to the Secretary of State and the Director of the Bureau of the Budget. The allowances regulations are a continuing consequence; the extension itself ended on revocation.
